article.title: は contraste
article.part: Arquitectura básica de la oración — 文の基本構造
article.chapter: Tópico, sujeto y contraste: は/が — 主題・主語・対比：は／が

claims.summary: Yoshimoto (1982) describes wa as having thematic and contrastive uses: thematic wa sets an element against the discourse background, while contrastive wa sets one element against another.

Kubota and Ido (2026) analyze Hanako-wa paatii-ni ki-ta as potentially conveying uncertainty about other attendees and sukunakutomo doo-medaru-wa toreru as a concessive weakening of a stronger claim; they distinguish contrastive wa from thematic wa and describe discourse alternatives as relevant.

locator.description: J-STAGE article overview, abstract (journal pp. 1–17): explicitly defines thematic wa as setting an element against discourse background and contrastive wa as setting one against another; DOI record lines 53–57.

links.notes: La redacción atribuye las definiciones a Yoshimoto, sin presentar una traducción fija.

locator.description: PDF pp. 1–2, introduction, examples (1a–b), lines 11–22: Hanako-wa paatii-ni ki-ta with uncertainty about others; (sukunakutomo) doo-medaru-wa toreru as concession; contrast with thematic wa and relevant wh-question discourse.
